analysis: The character equations solved over C (sympy) for all 256 codes give exactly six multiplicative characters - direct (0,1,0), strong (1,1,0), symmetric difference (1,-1,1), co-normal (1,0,1), code 127 (0,0,1), code 141 (1,1,-1) - and exactly two additive ones - Cartesian (0,t,0) and code 221 (0,0,t); identical to the hand case analysis; 0 numerical failures of the matrix identities on 30 random pairs per product; the Seidel spectrum of symmetric-difference products is multiplicative (shifted by 1) on 30/30 pairs. Only the empty and complete products among the 10 commutative associative ones have no character.
assumptions: characters solved exactly over C with sympy (independent of the hand case analysis)
numerical confirmation on 30 seeded random pairs of graphs with 1-5 vertices per product
falsification: A product outside the predicted lists with a solution, a predicted product without one, or a numerical failure of M_c(G*H) = M_c(G) (x) M_c(H).

hypothesis: H-C14-5 (derived by hand, Theorem 4/5 of proofs/paper/C14.md): exactly six products have a multiplicative character - direct (c=(0,1,0)), strong (1,1,0), co-normal (1,0,1), symmetric difference (1,-1,1), EA AE AA NN (1,1,-1) and the complement-dual of the direct product (0,0,1); exactly two have an additive character - Cartesian (0,1,0) and its complement-dual (0,0,1). H-C14-6 (bold): every commutative associative local product except the empty and complete products has a character of one of the two kinds.
methodology: Cell decomposition: A(G*H) = sum over cells in S of R_r1(G) (x) R_r2(H), R_E = I, R_A = A, R_N = J - I - A, with disjoint supports, all realised by P3 x P3; the functional equations reduce to polynomial equations in (c_E, c_A, c_N), solved by sympy for each of the 256 codes.
question: For which local products is there a matrix functor M_c(G) = c_E I + c_A A + c_N (J - I - A) (c_A != c_N) with M_c(G*H) = M_c(G) (x) M_c(H) (multiplicative character) or M_c(G*H) = M_c(G) (x) I + I (x) M_c(H) (additive character) for all graphs?
